title: Effects of Bedside Compared to Outside the Room Case Presentation
brief_summary: Patient case presentations during ward rounds can take place at the bedside or outside the room. The best approach to patient case presentation is yet unclear. Thus, the overall aim of this multicenter, randomized-controlled study is to test the hypothesis that outside the room patient case presentation compared to bedside patient case presentation results in better outcomes across different dimensions including patient understanding and perception of quality of care as well as patient outcomes, physicians' preferences, perception of quality and effectiveness, and timing of the ward rounds, respectively.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Consecutive adult (\>18 years) medical inpatients during their first ward round independently of their underlying disease and reason for hospital stay.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients with cognitive impairment, such as dementia/delirium
2. Patients with paracusia.
3. Patients who do not understand local language(s).
4. Patients already included in this study
